So, let's, I think, something I haven't asked you about is something about, is about the clarinet, you know, you have heard in New Orleans and ones that, you know, that made an impression on you, you know, different clarinet days you had when you were young.

But I tell you, I was a lot of them. But, uh, every one of them made an impression on me because, excuse me, every one had their own style. I was, uh, Charlie McQuirtis, P. Kool-Eddie's Betts, George Bakke, uh, Lorenzo Teal, uh, Johnny, uh, Johnny Brown, and so many others. Uh, and, uh, a lot of others that didn't…

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-10-21
items.q: That is Cherie, he played Albert.

ctx.x: Um, when you started playing clarinet, did all the clarinetists in New Orleans play Albert's system? Never. All of them. Were there, were the BAME systems around at that time?

I don't, I never saw him in the, I don't say, I never saw him. I know Israel Gorman, he played, he was pretty good on me. And then, at that time, he played Albert. Uh, uh, that is Cherie. That is Cherie, he played Albert. Uh, Zell, Zell, uh, Alondrie, which is, his niece, uh, lives around the corner there. He played Albert. George Abort, he played Albert. Uh, he, he also, and a lot of other fellas I know played Albert. Yeah. Uh, I use, I use the BAME system once, twice.
Why did you ever use a BAME system? Hmm? Why did you ever use a BAME system?
